name: Seven-Point Structure
description: Dan Wells' seven-point story structure in three acts, built on the reversal between hook and resolution. Four major turning points (plot turns, pinches, midpoint) steer the arc.

children.title: Hook
children.synopsis: Grab attention and establish the protagonist's ordinary start.

scenes.title: The Opening
scenes.synopsis: Create intrigue and a reason to read on.

children.title: Plot Turn 1
children.synopsis: The true adventure begins; the ordinary world is left behind.

scenes.title: The Shift
scenes.synopsis: The story's real direction snaps into place.

children.title: Pinch Point 1
children.synopsis: Apply pressure: the antagonist's power or the stakes become visible.

scenes.title: The Squeeze
scenes.synopsis: First proof of what's against the protagonist.

children.title: Midpoint
children.synopsis: A turn from reaction to action; a quest or mirror moment.

scenes.title: The Mirror
scenes.synopsis: The protagonist commits to the fight, often revealing theme.

children.title: Pinch Point 2
children.synopsis: Pressure peaks again; defeat feels close and the plan fractures.

scenes.title: The Break
scenes.synopsis: The antagonist shoves the protagonist toward the endgame.

children.title: Plot Turn 2
children.synopsis: The protagonist takes control and prepares the final push.

scenes.title: The Rally
scenes.synopsis: The protagonist turns the tables and sets the climax.

children.title: Resolution
children.synopsis: The climax pays off and the arc closes, mirroring the hook.

scenes.title: The Close
scenes.synopsis: Resolve the central conflict and land the change.
